41686223.model_description: A deep learning model segments the cerebellum on T2-weighted FLAIR infant brain MRI to quantify cerebellar volume; a brain-age-gap-like metric (predicted vs actual age from cerebellar volume) is used to detect cerebellar hypoplasia or atrophy.
41686223.dataset_size: 558 training scans; 492 normal + 40 abnormal validation scans
41686223.study_design: retrospective model development and validation using public and independent datasets

41686396.exclusion_reason: general rheumatology imaging review; AI mentioned only briefly as a future direction, not pediatric-focused

41688230.model_family: artificial neural network classifier on texture features
41688230.clinical_problem: predicting and diagnosing fetal growth restriction before clinical diagnosis
41688230.patient_population: 200 placental ultrasound images (100 FGR, 100 normal) at 20-24 weeks
41688230.model_description: Texture features (grayscale histogram, co-occurrence and run-length matrices, wavelet transform) extracted from second-trimester placental ultrasound images are fed into an artificial neural network to predict fetal growth restriction.
41688230.study_design: retrospective case-control study with train/test split

41689225.exclusion_reason: adult-only study; explicitly excludes pediatric radiographs

41692231.model_family: elastic-net penalized linear regression on radiomic features
41692231.clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes after neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
41692231.patient_population: 167 neonates (gestational age >=35 weeks) with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia
41692231.model_description: MRI-based radiomic measures from post-rewarming brain MRI in neonates with HIE are entered into an elastic-net regression model to predict 18-month Bayley cognitive, language, and motor developmental outcomes.
41692231.headline_result: mean correlation 0.94, predictive R2 0.87 between predicted and observed outcomes
41692231.study_design: retrospective single-center cohort study with 10-fold cross-validation

41692673.model_description: Corrigendum (correction notice) to a review article on deep learning applications in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research; no substantive abstract content is available.

41694946.exclusion_reason: general orthopedic disorders review; AI mentioned only in passing as a future technology

41695012.model_family: convolutional neural networks, ensemble learning, transfer learning (planned)
41695012.clinical_problem: predicting pre-eclampsia complications from obstetric Doppler ultrasound
41695012.patient_population: 150 pregnant women seeking obstetric ultrasound in Mbarara, Uganda, about half with pre-eclampsia
41695012.model_description: Study protocol to build an annotated Doppler obstetric ultrasound image dataset and train machine learning models (CNNs, ensemble and transfer learning) to predict maternal and fetal complications of pre-eclampsia.

41700557.clinical_problem: applying AI to point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency and critical care
41700557.model_description: Narrative review of AI-assisted point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric emergency/critical care, covering image acquisition assistance, diagnostic accuracy, education, and limitations of adult-trained models applied to children.

41702176.clinical_problem: automated quality control of fetal brain MRI stacks without quality labels
41702176.patient_population: fetal brain MRI atlases and clinical datasets (normal and abnormal fetuses)
41702176.model_description: OR-KAN predicts fetal MRI stack orientation (axial/sagittal/coronal) and uses the prediction uncertainty as a label-free image-quality score, used to select the highest-quality stacks for brain volume reconstruction.
41702176.dataset_size: seven fetal brain atlases plus TSE and BTFE clinical datasets
41702176.headline_result: AUROC 0.840 (TSE); improved brain reconstruction success rate from 64.4% to 83.2% (normal) and 60.0% to 85.5% (abnormal)
41702176.study_design: methods development and validation across two MRI sequence datasets

41706372.clinical_problem: assessing myelin maturation in infants from MRI
41706372.patient_population: 833 samples from a publicly available infant brain MRI dataset
41706372.model_description: A dual-input deep learning model fuses T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI features via cross-attention to predict myelin maturation age, with Grad-CAM interpretability.
41706372.study_design: retrospective model development using a public dataset

41707230.model_family: machine-learning-based predictive modeling of computational cognitive model parameters
41707230.clinical_problem: relating computational model parameters of response inhibition to task-related brain activation in children
41707230.patient_population: 9- to 11-year-olds from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (n=6469)
41707230.model_description: A formal computational (drift-diffusion-style) model of stop-signal task performance is related to fMRI task-activation via a machine-learning-based predictive modeling approach, in a large cohort of 9-11 year olds.
41707230.headline_result: variance explained R2 up to 26.86+/-1.69% for formal model parameters vs fMRI activation

41707249.clinical_problem: using AI to reduce CT radiation dose while preserving diagnostic performance, including in pediatric imaging
41707249.patient_population: 86 studies (2020-2025) covering chest, abdominal, vascular and pediatric CT applications
41707249.model_description: Narrative synthesis of 86 studies on AI-based CT dose optimization strategies (deep learning reconstruction, denoising, workflow automation such as auto-positioning), reporting dose reductions by anatomical region including a dedicated pediatric applications section.
41707249.headline_result: paediatric applications reported 50%-95% dose reductions; overall AI-based dose reductions of roughly 40%-90% across CT applications

41712150.exclusion_reason: adult cadaveric study, not diagnostic imaging AI in pediatric patients

41714232.clinical_problem: radiographic screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip in infants
41714232.patient_population: 1,188 anteroposterior pelvic radiographs of infants aged 2-12 months, Japan
41714232.model_description: A landmark-based deep learning system measures hip radiographic parameters and assigns International Hip Dysplasia Institute grades from infant pelvic radiographs, supporting a two-step triage strategy tested against pediatric orthopedic surgeon consensus.
41714232.headline_result: ICC 0.83-0.84 vs readers; triage sensitivity 0.75-0.93, specificity 0.62-0.95
41714232.study_design: retrospective model development with external evaluation

41714360.model_family: spectral-normalized GAN augmentation with ResNet18 + spatial attention classifier
41714360.patient_population: Pneumonia MNIST dataset, including pediatric lung images
41714360.model_description: A Double SGAN generative model addresses class imbalance in a pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset, and a ResNet18 classifier with spatial attention (ResNet18-SA) classifies images as pneumonia or normal.
41714360.dataset_size: Pneumonia MNIST dataset (size not specified in abstract)
41714360.study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset

41714423.model_family: deep-learning reconstruction combined with acceleration techniques
41714423.clinical_problem: enabling anesthesia-free emergency brain MRI in children by ruling out increased intracranial pressure or mass lesions
41714423.patient_population: 36 infants, median age 35.2 months, anesthesia-free imaging
41714423.model_description: Ultra-fast T2-weighted sequences combined with deep-learning reconstruction generate sub-minute (47-second) pediatric brain MRI, evaluated by four readers for diagnostic confidence in excluding midline shift or mass lesion.
41714423.headline_result: 94.4% of datasets at least acceptable diagnostic confidence; 72.6% good/excellent diagnostic confidence

41717559.model_family: machine learning variable selection (LASSO, random forest, stepwise/univariate regression) with graph-theoretical network analysis
41717559.clinical_problem: relating childhood chronic stress to brain white matter network abnormalities in adolescent depression
41717559.patient_population: 77 first-episode drug-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder and 31 healthy controls
41717559.model_description: T1-weighted and diffusion tensor imaging are used to build whole-brain white matter structural networks; graph-theoretical topological metrics are screened by machine learning methods (LASSO, random forest, etc.) and related to childhood chronic stress scores in adolescents with depression.

41718759.clinical_problem: multi-class diagnosis of neonatal lung diseases (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, pneumonia, pneumothorax, respiratory distress syndrome) from chest radiographs
41718759.patient_population: 2,089 neonates with clinical and imaging records
41718759.model_description: KD-SqueezeNet is a lightweight, knowledge-distilled deep learning model that classifies neonatal chest radiographs into five categories (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, pneumonia, pneumothorax, respiratory distress syndrome, normal).
41718759.headline_result: binary classification accuracy 0.93, AUROC 0.97; four-class accuracy 0.86
